name: gap-marker
description: The gap marker on disk (immortality §4.3: an explicit gap marker into the recording — wall-clock span and byte count lost; never splice silently; phase-01: a forced buffer overflow produces one). Frames 3 to 6 were lost while no core held the session's data socket; where they would have been, the recording holds one frame coded 2 whose data is a short fixed-format line (x-gap-line): 32 bytes lost, from the stamp of the last output frame the recording held (frame 2) to the stamp of the last frame lost (hello_ack's last_dropped_ts), and the frame is stamped with the span's end. A classic ttyrec player prints the line, so the recording tells the truth on its own; a TSB reader knows the marker by its code and parses the line. The byte count is the handshake's first_buffered_offset, 47, less the 15 bytes the recording held. Refused: an empty code-2 frame, data that is not the line, a line stamped elsewhere than its span's end, a span that ends before it starts. In a collected run every gap frame a tap holds has its marker, with the handshake's numbers.
